raw_response:
I'm 72 years old this year, been farming these fields for 50 years. My wife and I manage 6 mu together — just the two of us now, since our son works in Shijiazhuang and only comes back for holidays. I finished middle school, so when the extension technician comes to the village I can follow what he's saying, but honestly, after five decades I trust my own eyes more than his handouts.

This year I'm keeping my usual split: 4 mu in wheat-maize double cropping, and 2 mu in cotton. I thought about dropping the cotton since picking gets harder on my back every year, but the cotton price was decent last season and my neighbor Lao Zhang said the gin is buying again, so I'll keep the 2 mu.

The wheat went in last October like always — I bought an improved variety from the county supply store, cost me about 25 yuan per mu. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer and worked it in with the rotary tiller, about 25 kg per mu. The extension fellow told me 15 kg nitrogen per mu is enough, but my soil is decent and I know from experience that 16 kg works better here — I topdress with urea at jointing, about 12 kg per mu, and if the crop looks pale at heading I give it one more small shot. That's three applications total. I'll irrigate three times: I already did the winter irrigation in December, then one at jointing in March, and one more at grain filling in May. Water costs money — electricity for the pump keeps going up — but wheat is my main cash crop, so I don't skimp on it.

For the summer maize, it goes in mid-June right after wheat harvest. That window is brutal — sometimes only two or three days. I buy hybrid seed from the store, about 45 yuan per mu. I put all the fertilizer in the furrow at planting — about 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, which gives around 14 kg of nitrogen. No time for split application, the season is too short and I need to get it in fast before the soil dries. I usually irrigate twice if the summer rains don't come, but if July and August are wet I might only do it once. Maize gets herbicide and I'll watch for corn borers — if I see them, I spray insecticide.

The cotton on 2 mu gets planted in late April. I use an improved variety, about 40 yuan per mu for seed. Before planting I plow and harrow, then make ridges for drainage. I put down compound fertilizer, about 20 kg per mu, and side-dress with urea at flowering. Total nitrogen around 13 kg per mu. Cotton needs water — I'll irrigate twice, maybe three times if it's very dry. Pests are the big problem with cotton: herbicide for weeds, insecticide for bollworm, and sometimes fungicide if we get damp weather in August. The picking is what worries me now. My wife and I do the first picking ourselves, but last year my back gave out during the second picking and I had to hire a woman from the village for two days. Cost me 300 yuan but I had no choice. I'll probably need to do the same this year.

My total input costs this year will be about 1,540 yuan. That's a big number for us. I remember 2015 when I tried to save 200 yuan by cutting back on wheat fertilizer — then April turned dry and my yield dropped by nearly half. I lost ten times what I saved. So now I stick with what works, even if it hurts to pay for it up front. I expect about 400 kg per mu from the wheat, 450 kg per mu from the maize, and around 220 kg per mu of seed cotton if the weather holds. That's enough to feed us, pay for the inputs, and have a little left over. I'm not trying to get rich — I'm just trying to keep the farm going and not be a burden to my son.
